rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun was being swallowed at Moses’ prayer; though Qarun appealed to their kinship, Moses kept telling the earth to take him, and Qarun never called directly on God.
rows.anchor: وفيما أوحى الله إلى موسى : لقد ناداك بحق القرابة وأنت تقول : يا أرض خذيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says that when Jonah was held in the fish, God made the fish circle the seas with him until he reached Qarun; God then ordered that Qarun’s sinking not be increased because he had asked about his cousin Moses and maintained kinship.
rows.anchor: فلما حبس الله يونس في بطن الحوت أمر الحوت أن يطوف به في البحار لئلا يضيق قلب يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Admonition cannot benefit someone denied acceptance, just as seed cannot grow in saline ground; this explains why Qarun did not benefit from their advice.
rows.anchor: وعظ من حرم القبول كمثل البذر في الأرض السبخة ؛ ولذا لم ينفعه نصحهم إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person’s share of this world is neither to amass it all nor to renounce it all, but to take what benefits without later regret or punishment in the next life.
rows.anchor: ليس النصيب من الدنيا جمعها ولا منعها ، إنما النصيب منها ما تكون فيه فائدة بحيث لا يعقب ندما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inward reading makes worldly provisions a means to obey God with the self, know Him in the heart, remember Him with the tongue, and witness Him inwardly.
rows.anchor: ويقال النصيب من الدنيا ما يحمل على طاعته بالنفس ، وعلى معرفته بالقلب ، وعلى ذكره باللسان ، وعلى مشاهدته بالسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun could only have done good had he believed, since an unbeliever has no good deed in this sense.
rows.anchor: إنما كان يكون منه حسنة لو آمن بالله ؛ لأن الكافر لا حسنة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that God grants worldly blessings even to an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: والآية تدل على أن لله على الكافر نعما دنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded generosity is to spend blessings in obedience and service and answer them with gratitude rather than ingratitude.
rows.anchor: والإحسان الذي أمر به إنفاق النعمة في وجوه الطاعة والخدمة ، ومقابلته بالشكران لا بالكفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another inward sense of doing good is recognizing divine favor without imagining that one deserves it.
rows.anchor: ويقال الإحسان رؤية الفضل دون توهم الاستحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-admiration is ruinous; the deadly poison is looking at oneself as independently real and imagining that one possesses any power of negation or affirmation.
rows.anchor: ما لاحظ أحد نفسه إلا هلك بإعجابه . ويقال السم القاتل ، والذي يطفئ السراج المضيء النظر إلى النفس بعين الإثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People enamored of worldly life wished to possess what Qarun had, while those given knowledge judged God’s reward better for believers who act rightly and attainable only through patience.
rows.anchor: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا ولا يلقاهآ إلا الصابرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Qarun’s destruction, the people recognized God’s favor in keeping them from his way and its ruin.
rows.anchor: من الله علينا فلم ننجرف في نهجه ، ولم ننخرط في سلكه ، وإذا لوقع بنا الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who had coveted Qarun’s position regretted it; those content with God’s allotment were safe in this life, with their happiness to appear in the next.
rows.anchor: أما المتمنون مكانه فقد ندموا ، وأما الراضون بقسمته - سبحانه - فقد سلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One definition of worldly arrogance is imagining that someone else on earth is worse than oneself.
rows.anchor: قيل ( العلو في الدنيا ) أن تتوهم أن على البسيطة أحدا هو شر منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One definition of corruption is moving for the sake of one’s own appetite and share, even by a breath or a step; this exacting standard is for spiritual elites, while ordinary people are directed to the afterlife’s promise and warned against Pharaoh-like arrogance and Qarun-like corruption.
rows.anchor: و ( الفساد ) أن تتحرك لحظ نفسك ونصيبك ونصيبك ولو بنفس أو خطوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascetics seek no elevation on earth, while the gnostics seek no elevation in the afterlife or Paradise.
rows.anchor: ويقال الزهاد لا يريدون في الأرض علوا ، والعارفون لا يريدون في الآخرة والجنة علوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is the portion of worshippers and ascetics, whereas present mercy belongs to those marked by neediness and brokenness.
rows.anchor: ويقال { تلك الدار الأخرة } للعباد والزهاد ، وهذه الرحمة الحاضرة لأرباب الافتقار والانكسار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good deeds receive multiplication, while the treatment of evil deeds is based on mitigation.
rows.anchor: ثواب الحسنة في التضعيف ، وأمر السيئة بناؤه على التخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a believer with grave sins has sins outweighed by the greater good of faith and knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: والمؤمن - وإن كان صاحب كبائر - فسيئاته تقصر في جنب حسناته التي هي إيمانه ومعرفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, the promised return is to Mecca, fulfilling the Prophet’s repeated wish for his homeland.
rows.anchor: في الظاهر إلى مكة . . وكان يقول كثيرا : ( الوطن الوطن ) ، فحقق الله سؤله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the return is the soul’s state before embodiment, associated with intimations of nearness and encounters with the Real.
rows.anchor: والمعاد هو الوصف الذي كانت عليه روحك قبل حلول شجك من ملادغات القرب ومطالعات الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who established the Prophet in the differentiated duties of conveying and unfolding the law will return him to unitive realization of the Real and annihilation from creation.
rows.anchor: وقيل الذي ينصبك بأوصاف التفرقة بالتبليغ وبسط الشريعة لرادك إلى عين الجمع بالتحقق بالحق والفناء عن الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading says that the one who grounded him in the signs of servanthood will bring him to annihilation of self through effacement in the reality.
rows.anchor: ويقال إن الذي أقامك بشواهد العبودية فيما أثبتك به لرادك إلى الفناء عنك بمحقك في وجود الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet had not expected prophethood, the honor of the message, divine address, or the states of ecstasy and realized unity that God disclosed to him.
rows.anchor: ما كنت تؤمل محل النبوة وشرف الرسالة وتأهيل مخاطبتنا إليك ، ولا ما أظهرنا عليك من أحوال الوجد وحقائق التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not let the signs and states disclosed after revelation unsettle you or make you reject direct witnessing because scholars invoke rational possibilities; what sunlight reveals is not disproved by its obscurity in lamplight.
rows.anchor: لا يصدنك بعد إذ أنزلت إليك الآيات ما وجدته بحكم الذوب والشهود ، والإدراك والوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An act is vain unless done for God and to draw near to Him.
rows.anchor: كل عمل باطل إلا ما كان لوجه الله وللتقرب به إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every living thing is subject to death and nonexistence except God; the enduring mention of His Face entails the endurance of His essence and essential attributes, since an attribute cannot subsist without an existent essence.
rows.anchor: فكل شيء معد لجواز الهلاك والعدم ، ولا يبقى إلا { وجهه } : ووجهه صفة من صفاته لا تستقل إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Face is singled out because its permanence is known through revelation rather than reason; its remaining entails the Real’s permanence with all His attributes.
rows.anchor: وفائدة تخصيص الوجه بالذكر هنا أنه لا يعرف وجوب وجهه إلا بالخبر والنقل دون العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fulfill the conditions of prayer and the proper courtesies of worship are guided in this world and the next and attain deliverance.
rows.anchor: الذين يقومون بشرط صلاتهم وحق آداب عبادتهم هم الذين اهتدوا في الدنيا والعقبى فسلموا ونجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idle talk is whatever distracts from remembrance of God and whose hearing veils one from God.
rows.anchor: ما يشغل عن ذكر الله ، ويحجب عن الله سماعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls it empty outward speech that makes the inward heart heedless, engagement in falsehood, or taking up what does not concern one.
rows.anchor: هو لغو الظاهر الموجب سهو الضمائر ، وهو ما يكون خوضا فى الباطل ، وأخذا بما لا يعنيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person scattered in intention and heart grows more repelled by repeated admonition; such hearing is effectively no hearing and the counsel is wasted, as the poem says writing to a bored person is like writing on water.
rows.anchor: المفترق بهمه ، والمتشتت بقلبه لا تزيده كثرة الوعظ إلا نفورا ونبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief here means affirmation, and righteous action means realization; realization follows from affirmation, bringing safety and lasting rest.
rows.anchor: { ءامنوا } : صدقوا { وعملوا الصالحات } : تحققوا ؛ فاتصاف تحقيقهم راجع إلى تصديقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God holds the heavens by His power without pillars, supports, or pegs, through His decree, will, and governance.
rows.anchor: أمسك السموات بقدرته بغير عماد ، وحفظها لا إلى سناد أو مشدودة إلى أوتاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, the firmly set mountains are mountains; inwardly, they are the spiritual substitutes and pillars who aid creation and ward off calamity from near and far.
rows.anchor: في الظاهر الجبال ، وفي الحقيقة الأبدال والأوتاد الذين هم غياث الخلق ، بهم يقيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain from the outward heaven nourishes verdant gardens, while rain from the inward heaven nourishes the gardens of those brought near and present with God.
rows.anchor: المطر من سماء الظاهر في رياض الخضرة ؛ ومن سماء الباطن فى رياض أهل الدنو والحضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created heavens and earth display God’s majesty and expose the inability of those worshipped besides Him to create anything.
rows.anchor: هذا خلق الله العزيز في كبريائه ، فأروني ماذا خلق الذين عبدتم من دونه في أرضه وسمائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is sound judgment in intellect, belief, and speech.
rows.anchor: { الحكمة } الإصابة في العقل والعقد والنطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is following the path through divine enabling rather than the self’s own effort.
rows.anchor: ويقال { الحكمة } متابعة الطريق من حيث توفيق الحق لا من حيث همة النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom means not falling under the rule of caprice.
rows.anchor: ويقال { الحكمة } ألا تكون تحت سلطان الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is living according to the judgment of the One who possesses judgment.
rows.anchor: ويقال { الحكمة } الكون بحكم من له الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom includes knowing one’s own measure and not extending oneself beyond one’s covering.
rows.anchor: ويقال { الحكمة } معرفة قدر نفسك حتى لا تمد رجليك خارجا عن كسائك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom means not resisting someone whom one knows one cannot withstand.
rows.anchor: ويقال { الحكمة } ألا تستعصي على من تعلم أنك لا تقاومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reality of gratitude is the heart’s eye opening to witness the Lord’s gentle favors.
rows.anchor: حقيقة الشكر انفراج عين القلب بشهود ملاطفات الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source links shukr with kashr through a reversal of letters, as in the paired forms shakar/kashara and jazaba/jabaza.
rows.anchor: فيقال شكر وكشر مثل جذب وجبذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is realizing one’s incapacity to thank God adequately.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشكر تحققك بعجزك عن شكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is what completes one’s enjoyment of a blessing.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشكر ما به يحصل كمال استلذاذ النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is praise flowing from a heart so filled with joy that the tongue praises the one thanked.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشكر فضلة تظهر على اللسان من امتلاء القلب بالسرور ؛ فينطلق بمدح المشكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude marks every truly rich person, while ingratitude marks every ignoble person.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشكر نعت كل غني كما أن الكفران وصف كل لئيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude knocks at the door of increase and serves as a bond that holds blessings.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشكر قرع باب الزيادة . ويقال الشكر قيد الإنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is a story the heart’s core dictates by publishing a record of divine favors.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشكر قصة يمليها صميم الفؤاد بنشر صحيفة الأفضال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who gives thanks benefits their own soul, because gratitude advances its welfare and share.
rows.anchor: لأنه في صلاحها ونصيبها يسعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is divided into overt idolatry and hidden shirk, which includes attributing events to created people or affirming another alongside God while witnessing the unseen.
rows.anchor: الشرك على ضربين : جلي وخفي ؛ فالجلي عبادة الأصنام ، والخفي حسبان شيء من الحدثان من الأنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition calls shirk affirming anything other than God while witnessing the unseen.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشرك إثبات غير مع شهود الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk wrongs the heart, whereas sins wrong the self; wrongs of the self may be forgiven, but there is no avenue to forgiveness for wronging the heart.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشرك ظلم على القلب ، والمعاصي ظلم على النفس ، وظلم النفوس معرض للغفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since consensus holds that gratitude to parents requires sustained obedience, not merely verbal praise, gratitude to God likewise requires obedience and using blessings in obedience rather than sin; God is thanked through glorification, parents through provision.
rows.anchor: علم أن شكر الحق لا يكفي فيه مجرد القول ما لم تكن فيه موافقه العقل ؛ وذلك بالتزام الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshipped beings cannot benefit others; at the Resurrection they disavow their worshippers’ association, but belief then is useless after the period of moral responsibility has ended.
rows.anchor: { ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم } : لا يؤمنون إلا في ذلك الوقت ، ولكن لا ينفعهم الإيمان بعد زوال التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are two kinds of poverty: essential poverty of created nature and poverty as a spiritual quality.
rows.anchor: الفقر على ضربين : فقر الخلقة وفقر الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Essential poverty is universal: every creature needs its Creator to bring it from nonbeing into existence and then to sustain and preserve it.
rows.anchor: فكل مخلوق مفتقر إلى خالقه ، فهو قد حصل من العدم ، فهو مفتقر إليه ليبديه وينشيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poverty as a spiritual quality is detachment: ordinary people detach from wealth, while the elect detach from impediments so that their poverty may be sound.
rows.anchor: وأما فقر الصفة فهو التجرد ، ففقر العوام التجرد من المال ، وفقر الخواص التجرد من الأعلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may be needy toward God or toward something that comes from God; dependence on a thing is a kind of self-sufficiency through that thing, while need of God is richness through God, and each entails the other.
rows.anchor: ومن افتقر إلى شيء استغنى بوجود ذلك الشيء ؛ فالفقير إلى الله هو الغني بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poverty is ennobled by humility and submission, while wealth can be marred by pride; the servant’s honor lies in poverty and abasement in imagining oneself self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: ومن شرف الفقر اقترانه بالتواضع والخضوع ، ومن آفات الغنى امتزاجه بالتكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blameworthy poverty is when God veils a person from seeing where they need Him; praiseworthy poverty is when God makes those places of need visible.
rows.anchor: ومن الفقر المذموم ، أن يستر الحق على صاحبه مواضع فقره إلى ربه ، ومن الفقر المحمود أن يشهده الحق مواضع فقره إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sincere poor person owns nothing yet owns everything; more precisely, no thing possesses the truly poor person.
rows.anchor: ومن شرط الفقير المخلص ألا يملك شيئا ويملك كل شيء . ويقال : الفقير الصادق الذي لا يملكه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sincere poor person’s courtesy is to show gratitude at the height of being broken.
rows.anchor: ومن آداب الفقير الصادق إظهار التشكر عند كمال التكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The etiquette of poverty is completeness of spiritual meaning and the disappearance of self-claim.
rows.anchor: ومن آداب الفقر كمال المعنى وزوال الدعوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another practice is to be grateful in affliction and refrain from complaint.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشكر على البلوى والبعد عن الشكوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reality of praiseworthy poverty is stripping the innermost self of causal attachments and making the heart exclusively God’s.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الفقر المحمود تجرد السر عن المعلولات وإفراد القلب بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praiseworthy poverty is living with God in the ease of an unoccupied inward state throughout time, without resisting any condition.
rows.anchor: ويقال : الفقر المحمود العيش مع الله براحة الفراغ على سرمد الوقت من غير استكراه شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s self-description as rich and praiseworthy signals that He gives until He is praised.
rows.anchor: الإشارة منه أن يعطي حتى يحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created beings display wealth either to boast or outdo others, or to give generously; God is far above the first motives, so His declaration of human poverty signals generosity rather than belittlement.
rows.anchor: وإنما المقصود أنه إذا قال : والله الغني ، وأنتم الفقراء أنه يجود علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one does not claim self-sufficiency, which belongs to God, God grants what enriches and gives beyond what is sufficient.
rows.anchor: ويقال إذا لم تدع ما هو صفته - من استحقاق الغنى - أولاك ما يغنيك ، وأعطاك فوق ما يكفيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Today God has made the body’s limbs serve one another, but tomorrow He will overturn this custom and make them dispute; unbelievers’ limbs testify against them, while sinful believers may have some limbs testify against them and others for them.
rows.anchor: اليوم سخر الله أعضاء بدن الإنسان بعضها لبعض ، وغدا ينقض هذه العادة ، فتخرج بمض الأعضاء على بعض ، وتجري بينها الخصومة والنزاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ungraded report says that when a servant’s limbs testify to a sin, an eyelash hair asks leave to testify that it witnessed the servant’s tears of fear; God forgives him, and a herald calls him freed by a single hair.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار المروية المسندة أن عبدا تشهد عليه أعضاؤه بالزلة فيتطاير شعره من جفن عينيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After youth and strength, a person declines toward the weakness of childhood in extreme old age; this applies to bodies and structures, while inward states and meanings can continue to grow.
rows.anchor: يرده إذا استوى شبابه وقوته إلى العكس ، فكما كان يزداد في القوة يأخذ في النقصان إلى أن يبلغ أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual states grow until senility disrupts judgment, but people of spiritual realities may gray physically while their love and inward meanings remain fresh and youthful.
rows.anchor: وأهل الحقائق تشيب ذوائبهم ولكن محابهم ومعانيهم في عنفوان شبابها ، وطراوة جدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s speech was outside poetic meters, and the Qur’an was neither poetry nor a method of oratory; opponents were baffled because their sight lacked the light of tawhid and could not witness realities.
rows.anchor: والذي أتاهم به من القرآن لم يكن من أنواع الشعر ، ولا من طرق الخطباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s favor in livestock includes riding, meat and fat, milk, carrying loads, covering distances, wool, fur, hair, and even bones; this demands gratitude, in which people fall short.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم ينتفعون بركوبها وبأكل لحومها وشحومها ، وبشرب ألبانها ، وبالحمل عليها ، وقطع المسافات بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite these many benefits, people made beings like themselves their gods; if such ingratitude characterized a creature, it would amount to complaint.
rows.anchor: أنهم مع كل هذه الوجوه من الإحسان : - اكتفوا بأمثالهم معبودات لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God consoles the Prophet not to grieve over his opponents’ words, since God knows what they conceal and reveal.
rows.anchor: فلا يحزنك قولهم إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing that God sees him makes the servant’s suffering easier to bear, especially suffering for God’s sake.
rows.anchor: وإذا علم العبد أنه بمرأى من الحق هان عليه ما يقاسيه ، ولا سيما إذا كان في الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tightly joined, assembled, and proportioned human limbs and endowed people with reason and discrimination, yet the human becomes an explicit disputant who argues against divine rulings as if his own judgment were sound.
rows.anchor: شدّدنا أسرهم ، وجمعنا نشرهم ، وسوينا أعضاءهم ، وركبنا أجزاءهم ، وأودعناهم العقل والتمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human’s argumentative ingratitude is like the pupil who, after being taught archery until strong, turns his bow against his teacher.
rows.anchor: أعلمه الرماية كل يوم . . . فلما اشتد ساعده رماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is no more difficult than initial creation; the One who produces fire in green branches can give life to rotten bones, and His ability to create a likeness is His ability to create the thing itself.
rows.anchor: وقال إن الإعادة في معنى الإبداء ، فأي إشكال بقي في جواز الإعادة في الانتهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revives souls after death as He creates humans from sperm and birds from eggs; He also gives believing hearts life through gnosis and kills unbelievers’ souls through desire and tyranny.
rows.anchor: وإنه يحيي النفوس بعد موتها في العرصة كما يحيي الإنسان من النطفة ، والطير من البيضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills a thing, His command “Be” brings it into existence through His creation and power; producing many or few is equally easy for Him.
rows.anchor: يخلقه وقدرته . وأخبرنا أنه تتعلق بالمكون كلمته على ما يجب في صفته ، وسيان عنده خلق الكثير في كثرته والقليل في قلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything appears by God’s power and only continues by His sustaining; He originates what comes to be, and all created things return to Him.
rows.anchor: فلا يحدث شيء - قل أو كثر - إلا بإبداعه وإنشائه ، ولا يبقى منها شيء إلا بإبقائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those guided to God’s oneness are people of sound understanding.
rows.anchor: أولئك الذين هداهم الله لتوحيده ، وأولئك الذين عقولهم غير معقولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those decreed punishment include people sentenced to the Fire and people sentenced to the punishment of being veiled from God today; they remain trapped behind their heart’s veil, even if they belong outwardly to the faithful.
rows.anchor: فريق حقت عليهم كلمة بعذابهم في النار ، وفريق حقت عليهم كلمة العذاب بالحجاب اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promises of Paradise to the obedient, forgiveness to the repentant, and presence and arrival to seekers are certain, provided seekers do not lapse into an intervening pause.
rows.anchor: وعد المطيعين بالجنة - ولا محالة لا يخلف ، ووعد التائبين بالمغفرة - ولا محالة يغفر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, rain makes vegetation green before it dries and becomes stubble; inwardly, this is the human life course from childhood through age and decrepitude to death.
rows.anchor: أخبر أنه ينزل من السماء المطر فيخرج به الزرع فيخضر ، ثم يأخذ في الجفاف ، ثم يصير هشيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grain is the crop’s purpose and is not gathered until the plant begins to dry; likewise, a person has no worth until they attain arrival.
rows.anchor: ويقال إن الزرع ما لم يأخذ في الجفاف لا يؤخذ منه الحب ، فالحب هو المقصود منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer’s intellect first advances knowledge until insight reaches fullness; then the dawning authority of divine knowledge submerges those lights, and the lights of tawhid consume them all.
rows.anchor: كذلك الإنسان ما لم يحصل من نفسه وصول لا يكون له قدر ولا قيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the lights of tawhid appear, they absorb the prior lights of insight, as sunrise enfolds the light of the stars.
rows.anchor: فإذا بدت أنوار التوحيد استهلكت تلك الجملة ، قالوا : فلما استبان الصبح أدرج ضوءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to the verse’s implied comparison is omitted: is the one whose breast God expands for Islam like the one whose breast is not expanded?
rows.anchor: جواب هذا الخطاب محذوف . . . أي أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام كمن ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: الرسول - صلى الله عيله وسلم -
rows.claim: The Prophet explained the breast’s expansion as a light cast into the heart; its sign is turning away from the delusive world toward the eternal home and preparing for death before it arrives.
rows.anchor: لما نزلت هذه الآية سئل الرسول - صلى الله عيله وسلم - عن الشرح المذكور فيها ، فقال : ( ذلك نور يقذف في القلب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine light unfolds through successive stations: signs of knowledge, clarity of understanding, added certainty, disclosure of attributes, witnessing of the Essence, and the realities of tawhid; beyond these, ordinary categories of presence and absence or nearness and distance fall away.
rows.anchor: ثم نور المكاشفة بتجلي الصفات ، ثم نور المشاهدة بظهور الذات ، ثم أنوار الصمدية بحقائق التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hard hearts are those not struck by intimations of recognition, remaining in denial, enduring error, and lasting ignorance.
rows.anchor: اي الصلبة قلوبهم ، لم تقرعها خواطر التعريف فبقيت على نكرة الجحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is the best discourse because it is uncreated.
rows.anchor: { أحسن الحديث } لأنه غير مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is called mutually similar because of its inimitability and eloquence.
rows.anchor: { كتابا متشابها } في الإعجاز والبلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated passages set out judgments without tiring the reader and include praise of God’s sovereignty and beneficence, descriptions of Paradise and Hell, and promises and threats.
rows.anchor: يثني فيها الحكم ولا يمل بتكرار القراءة ، ويشتمل على نوعين : الثناء عليه بذكر سلطانه وإحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warnings make those who fear their Lord shudder, while promises make their skin and hearts soften toward remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم } إذا سمعوا آيات الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shuddering and softening may be read as fear and hope, contraction and expansion, awe and intimacy, or divine disclosure and concealment.
rows.anchor: ويقال : تقشعر وتلين بالخوف والرجاء ، ويقال بالقبض والبسط ، ويقال بالهيبة والأنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison asks whether one who shields himself with his face from punishment is like one who does not; the unbeliever is thrown into the Fire face-first, while the believer is spared and meets radiance, joy, and honor.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الكافر يلقى النار أول ما يلقاها بوجهه ؛ لأنه يرمى فيها منكوسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severest punishment arrives unexpectedly, just as the fullest joy comes suddenly; unexpected estrangement and separation wound the heart most deeply.
rows.anchor: أشد العذاب ما يكون بغتة ، كما أن أتم السرور ما يكون فلتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most complete and affecting joy is also the joy that comes by surprise.
rows.anchor: وأتم السرور وأعظمه تأثيرا ما يكون فجأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the signs clear and acquainted people with the realities of things; the Book has no crookedness and cannot be reached by falsehood from either direction.
rows.anchor: أي أوضحنا لهم الآيات ، ووقفناهم على حقائق الأشياء . { غير ذى عوج } : فلا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheist resembles a slave disputed by quarrelsome partners, each claiming the servant; the monotheist resembles a slave devoted to one master and free of conflict.
rows.anchor: مثل الكافر ومعبوديه بعبد اشترك فيه متنازعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divided servant is pulled among worldly concerns such as children, family, and other distracting thoughts; the believer is wholly God’s, with no worldly claim or deeds on which to rely.
rows.anchor: تتجاذبه أشغال الدنيا ، شغل الولد وشغل العيال ، وغير ذلك من الأشغال المختفلة والخواطر المشتتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s words to Moses, “I chose you for Myself,” mean that He kept Moses for Himself so that he would be fit for no other.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى لموسى : { واصطنعتك لنفسى } [ طه : 41 ] أي أبقيتك لي حتى لا تصلح لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All praise belongs to God, who is entitled to the attributes of majesty.
rows.anchor: الثناء له ، وهو مستحق لصفات الجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of night and day and the courses of sun and moon are signs of God’s power and proofs of His oneness.
rows.anchor: واختلاف الليل والنهار ، ودوران الشمس والقمر من جملة أمارات قدرته ، ودلالات توحيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun’s height and the moon’s brightness are no grounds for worship; God is jealous for the servant’s devotion and commands prostration to their Creator.
rows.anchor: في علائها ، { ولا للقمر } في ضيائه ، { واسجدوا لله } فقد غار عليك أن تسجد لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although sun and moon are lofty and beautiful, they were created for human benefit, so people should worship their Creator rather than them.
rows.anchor: والشمس - وإن علت ، والقمر - وإن حسن . . . فلأجلك خلقناهما ، فلا تسجد لهما ، واسجد لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded the angels, despite their abundant worship and precedence in obedience, to bow to Adam; by contrast, He tells sinful human descendants not to bow to sun and moon.
rows.anchor: خلق الملائكة - ومع كثرة عبادتهم ، ومع تقدمهم في الطاعة - قال لهم : اسجدوا لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to protect one’s face from sun and moon exposes the indignity of moving one’s feet for every base desire and presenting oneself before everyone.
rows.anchor: والحق - سبحانه وتعالى - يأمرك بصيانة وجهك عن الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If unbelievers refuse worship, God loses nothing, for He needs no one; the angels, inhabitants of the hereafter, worship Him tirelessly night and day.
rows.anchor: أي إن ترفع الكفار فلا خلل ؛ لأن الحق غني عن كل أحد ، ثم إن الملائكة - الذين هم سكان الآخر - يسجدون له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As rain revives parched winter earth, awareness of sin humbles hearts; God turns toward them, bringing the blessings of regret and forgiving their failures in sincerity.
rows.anchor: وكذلك القلوب إذا خشعت لاستشعارها بما ألمت به من الذنوب أقبل عليها الحق سبحانه ، فظهر فيها بركات الندم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a servant lapses in spiritual practice or leaves the ground of obedience, God’s reminder brings lights of concord, restores the accustomed station, and makes the branch of fidelity fresh again.
rows.anchor: ثم تغمده الحق - سبحانه - بما يدخل عليه من التذكر تظهر في القلب أنوار الوفاق ، فيعود إلى مألوف مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If gnostics pause or suffer a veil because of bad etiquette, God’s caring regard makes their gardens of intimacy stir, their scenes of nearness green, and their impediments retreat.
rows.anchor: وكذلك إذا بدت لأهل العرفان وقفة ، أو حدثت لهم من جراء سوء أدب بدر منهم حجبة ثم نظر الحق - سبحانه - إليهم بالرعاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who revives dead earth can raise the dead, and He can also revive hearts with the light of care after spiritual slackness and veiling.
rows.anchor: إن الذي أحيا الأرض بعد موتها قادر على إحياء النفوس بالحشر والنشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers will receive the punishment they deserve; whatever they choose to do only advances their condemnation and carries them toward ruin.
rows.anchor: فليعملوا ما شاءوا . . فليسوا . . يسعون إلا في ذمهم ، وليسوا يمشون إلا إلى هلاكهم بأقدامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unstated consequence for those who reject the Reminder is that they are left behind, disgraced, and wretched forever.
rows.anchor: الجواب محذوف ومعناه : بقوا عنا ، ووقعوا في هوانهم وشقوا إلى الأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is “mighty” because it has no equal, overcomes the suspicions of innovators and unbelievers, and cannot be matched by anyone.
rows.anchor: كتاب عزيز لا مثل له حيث قد عجزوا عن الإتيان بمثله . كتاب عزيز غالب لشبه المبتدعين والكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also mighty because it is the speech of a mighty Lord, conveyed to a mighty messenger by a mighty angel for a mighty community.
rows.anchor: كتاب عزيز لأنه كلام رب عزيز إلى رسول عزيز بسفارة ملك عزيز إلى أمة عزيزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For believers, the Qur’an is mighty and beloved because it is the speech of their beloved.
rows.anchor: كتاب عزيز على المؤمنين لأنه كتاب حبيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast implies that sinful believers may be punished, but their punishment is not severe like that of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فالعصاة من المؤمنين لهم عذاب . . اما الكافرون فلهم عذاب شديد ؛ لأن دليل الخطاب يقتضي هذا وذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if fear of Hell or hope for Paradise does not move someone to repent, they should repent because God accepts the repentant.
rows.anchor: إن لم يتب العبد خوفا من النار ، ولا طمعا في الجنة لكان من حقه أن يتوب ليقبل الحق - سبحانه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sinner remains brokenhearted and longs for an easy deed God will accept; God answers that if the sinner has no acceptable deed, repentance can still be made acceptable.
rows.anchor: إن العاصي يكون ابدا منكسر القلب ، فإذا علم أن الله يقبل الطاعة من المطيعين يتمنى أن ليت له طاعة ميسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse sounds outwardly like a human apology: God did not expand a poor servant’s provision because He knew abundance would make the servant transgress and spread corruption.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنني لم أبسط عليك أيها الفقير في الدنيا لما كان لي من العلم أنني لو قسمت عليك الدنيا لطغيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adversative “but” corrects the idea that God either grants all one wants or withholds everything: He apportions provision as He wills.
rows.anchor: ولم أمنع عنك ( الكل ) ؛ لأني أنزل بقدر ما أشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, when people despair of rain and the land is drought-stricken, God sends rain near the point when hope is lost and revives the earth with mercy.
rows.anchor: بعدما أصاب الأرض جدوبة ، وأبطأ نزول الغيث ، وقنط الناس من مجيء المطر ، وأشرف الوقت على حد الفوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also revives hearts: when the branch of one’s spiritual time withers, love clouds over, intimacy dims, and nearness recedes, divine mercy may rain upon the innermost self and renew intimacy.
rows.anchor: فلربما ينظر إليه الحق برحمته ؛ فينزل على سره أمطار الرحمة ، ويعود عوده طريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem hopes that estrangement will end, old covenants will live again, and a withered branch will turn green and sway.
rows.anchor: ولعل عهدك باللوى . . . يحيا فقد تحيا العهود والغصن ييبس تارة . . . وتراه مخضرا يميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every created thing points to God’s oneness in majesty and uniqueness in grandeur and beauty.
rows.anchor: جعل الله في كل شيء من الخلوقات دلالة على توحده في جلاله ، وتفرده بنعت كبريائه وجماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s gathering of all people has an inward sign: divine jealousy prevents the saints’ hearts from settling on one another, so their gatherings are repeatedly dispersed and rarely last long.
rows.anchor: أن الحق - سبحانه - يغار على أوليائه أن يسكن بعضهم بقلبه إلى بعض ؛ فأبدا يبدد شملهم
